page: Microsoft Azure D16s_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine deployed on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by a dedicated 2.8 GHz Intel Xeon Platinum 8370C processor built on the x86_64 architecture. It features 16 vCPUs derived from 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core, backed by 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 48 MB of L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX, AVX-512F, and AVX-512 VNNI, along with cryptographic hardware acceleration such as AES, VAES, and SHA-NI. The server provides 64.0 GB of memory, maintaining a 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. No dedicated GPUs or local storage devices are bundled, relying entirely on remote storage configurations.

Benchmark results demonstrate reliable mid-tier performance across varied computational tasks. The instance scored 1,625.0 in Geekbench single-core and 9,869.0 in multi-core metrics, alongside a PassMark CPU score of 21,254.08 and a stress-ng multi-core rating of 15,535.78. Memory bandwidth reaches 99.68 GB/sec for large uncached reads and 56.31 GB/sec for uncached writes, resulting in a PassMark memory score of 2,717.94. Data throughput benchmarks show strong multi-threaded decompression at 44.88 GB/sec via bzip3 and 28.54 GB/sec for single-threaded gzip compression. While medium-model (7B) LLM text generation operates at an average 12.27 tokens per second, text generation on a lightweight 135M model registers a strong 285.04 tokens per second.

The 1:4 core-to-memory configuration delivers qualitative cost efficiency for resource-balanced production workloads, avoiding the overhead of specialized acceleration hardware when not required. Tradeoffs include the total absence of onboard local scratch storage, meaning all disk operations must route over the network to attached volumes. The lack of AMX instructions and hardware GPUs also prevents deployment for large-scale AI training. Microsoft Azure D16s_v5 is best suited for medium enterprise web serving, backend relational and in-memory databases, continuous integration build pipelines, and general business application tiers.

Featuring an 8-core, 16-thread layout with 48 MB of L3 cache, the system includes AVX-512 and hardware cryptographic support. It carries no local storage or GPUs, relying on attached remote storage. Across synthetic benchmarks, it presents balanced middle-tier results, such as a Geekbench multi-core score of 9,869.0, a PassMark CPU score of 21,254.08, and Redis set operations reaching 15.61 million operations per second. Memory throughput reaches 99.68 GB/sec for large uncached reads. The configuration provides balanced resource density for enterprise application tiers, web serving, CI/CD compilation, and mid-sized databases.
